title: Auction Expense Allowance on TRAC Deficiencies — Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease
content:
# Auction Expense Standard — Sale Expenses Allowed on a TRAC Deficiency, Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

**Standard.** For the deficiency billed on a TRAC unit of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease whose sale settlement falls short of its book value, the sale expenses allowed follow how soon the unit sold after its turn-in: for a sale 30 or fewer days after the turn-in date, the lesser of the actual sale expenses and 5 percent of the gross sale proceeds; for a sale 31 to 60 days after the turn-in date, the lesser of the actual sale expenses and 8 percent of the gross sale proceeds; for a later sale, the actual sale expenses.

**Records read.** The unit's turn-in date and sale date, and the actual sale expenses and gross sale proceeds on the sale settlement. Days run from the turn-in date to the sale date and count the later date but not the earlier one. The percentage limit is the gross sale proceeds multiplied by 5 (or 8) and divided by 100.

| Days from turn-in date to sale date | Sale expenses allowed |
|---|---|
| 30 or fewer | the lesser of the actual sale expenses and 5 percent of the gross sale proceeds |
| 31 to 60 | the lesser of the actual sale expenses and 8 percent of the gross sale proceeds |
| more than 60 | the actual sale expenses |

## Cases (hypothetical: gross sale proceeds 16000.00, actual sale expenses 1100.00)

| Days to sale | Limit | Allowed |
|---|---|---|
| 30 | 5 percent: 800.00 | 800.00 |
| 31 | 8 percent: 1280.00 | 1100.00 (actual is lower) |
| 60 | 8 percent: 1280.00 | 1100.00 |
| 61 | none | 1100.00 |

With actual sale expenses of 600.00 and a sale 20 days after turn-in, the allowed figure is 600.00, the actual expenses being below the 800.00 limit.
